[[Siege Turtle]]s are massive reptiles with cannons mounted on their backs. These [[siege weapon]]s are exclusively used by the [[Luxon]]s and have the same [[spirit range|range]] as passive spirits. Their durability is increased by [[Turtle Shell]] and [[Carrier Defense]].

==Notes==
*When using its Siege Turtle Attack, the turtle is resistant to [[interrupt]]ion. Only every third interruption attempt will successfully interrupt the turtle. These attempts do not have to be made during the same siege attack.
*[[Juggernaut Toss]] will flip the turtles over, drastically reducing their [[armor rating]] (down to around AR 20) and temporarily nullifying their [[Turtle Shell]]. 
*They do not show any animation when [[knocked down]] (and they do not suffer the penalties associated with being flipped over by a [[Juggernaut]]).
*Their [[aggro]] radius is about [[spirit range]].
*The Siege Turtles in [[Fort Aspenwood]] will not move if any non-[[summon]]ed enemy is within their siege attack [[range]] (slightly smaller than the range of most [[spirit]]s) until the enemy moves out of range, moves into [[nearby]] range, or is killed.
*The Fort Aspenwood version has 72 armor against at least [[elemental damage]] and [[slashing damage]].

==Trivia==
*It has a miniature version: the [[Miniature Siege Turtle]].
*In ancient Japanese mythology, there were gigantic turtles that carried heavy loads, much like the Siege Turtles.
*Siege turtles like [[Feedback:Game_updates/20100302|carrots]].
*The siege turtle appears to be a giant version of a [[w:Galápagos tortoise|Galápagos tortoise]].
* [[Guild Wars 2]] has a mounted version of the [[gw2:Siege Turtle|Siege Turtle]] based on this NPC.
